body.name: the endpoint-preserving cycle-compression handle
body.construction: Use the fully specified normalized instance \(\zeta_\star\) at \(v=0\). Fix \(z=w=1\), parameterize the repeated corner word \((0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1)\) by \(\boldsymbol\theta\), and evaluate \(\Phi\) and \(\mathcal G_0\) exactly by \(E(g,\ell)\). At every normal stationary point satisfying \(\nabla\mathcal G_0=D\Phi^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\mu\), compute \(\mathscr Q\). A compression certificate is a \(C^2\) curve \(\boldsymbol\theta(s)\) with \(\Phi(\boldsymbol\theta(s))=0\), \(\mathcal G_0'(0)=0\), \(\mathcal G_0''(0)>0\) for the upper problem, and a finite \(s_1\) at which one duration vanishes while \(\mathcal G_0(\boldsymbol\theta(s_1))\ge\mathcal G_0(\boldsymbol\theta(0))\); locally, \(\lambda_{\max}(\mathscr Q)>0\) is the exact improving-direction sign. An obstruction certificate is an interior \(\boldsymbol\theta\in\mathcal T_\star\) with \(\mathscr Q\preceq0\) and the exact strict separation \(\mathcal G_0(\boldsymbol\theta)=\max_{\boldsymbol\eta\in\overline{\mathcal T}_\star}\mathcal G_0(\boldsymbol\eta)>\max_{\boldsymbol\eta\in\partial\overline{\mathcal T}_\star}\mathcal G_0(\boldsymbol\eta)\); reverse the Hessian and objective inequalities for the lower problem. After this kill test, treat flat, single-control singular, abnormal, and boundary phases by endpoint-preserving pulse replacement and compact limiting arguments.
